summary: Iteration 46 — Cloudflare Turnstile CAPTCHA on /auth/login and /auth/register. Backend: 10/10 pytest pass (login + register both gated, exact 'Security verification failed. Please try again.' message returned with HTTP 400 for missing token, bogus token, and whitespace token; register failure verified to NOT persist a user in db.users; regression on /api/campaigns, /api/drip-campaigns, /api/dne-lists, /api/unibox/replies, /api/accounts all return 200 with session cookie). Frontend: Turnstile widget renders on both /login and /register (visually confirmed via screenshot — 'Verify you are human' + Cloudflare branding), wrapper testids login-turnstile-wrapper and register-turnstile-wrapper present, turnstile-container present, the Cloudflare api.js script is injected exactly ONCE per page load, both login-submit-btn and register-submit-btn are disabled before the challenge is solved. Secret-key audit: fetched all 10 JS bundles referenced from /login and grep'd them — TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY (0x4AAAAAADgY3dK_B7t1fZDG7db_iCbUzpk) does NOT appear in any bundle or in the DOM; only the SITE key (0x4AAAAAADgY3RGHODsGMCYW) is in the bundle (expected). Mobile responsiveness at 390x844: scrollWidth==innerWidth==390 on both /login and /register, no horizontal overflow. Code review of /app/backend/server.py confirms verify_turnstile_or_raise is defined at L1999 and is the FIRST line of both /auth/login (L2855) and /auth/register (L2468), before user lookup / password hash check / DB insert.
critical_code_review_comments: verify_turnstile_or_raise silently skips when TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY env is unset/empty (dev-mode bypass). Intentional per the code comment and the iteration spec, but it is a foot-gun for production: if the env var is ever blanked accidentally the CAPTCHA gate disappears with no error. Suggest a startup-time assertion or a separate TURNSTILE_REQUIRED=true flag for production deployments — non-blocking for iter-46.

Turnstile.jsx: the useEffect dependency array intentionally omits onToken/onExpire/onError to support inline-lambda parents. This is fine but leaves a comment-only contract; if a parent ever swaps callbacks at runtime the old ones will continue to fire. Low risk because Login/Register both use stable setState setters via closure, but worth a JSDoc note. Non-blocking.

Pre-existing lint blockers in Login.jsx / Register.jsx (apostrophes, react-hooks immutability) are carried over from earlier iterations and were explicitly excluded from iter-46 scope per the request. Confirmed not regressed.
